subject: DPA: territory controls, BYOK responsibilities, and operator access limits
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@veridianhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Thompson <jill@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on DPA boundaries & BYOK for private deployment

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we dig into procurement, Legal and Security are asking for a clean summary of how the DPA will reflect:

- Territory / cross-border transfer controls for data stored in our private VPC and for backups
- Who is the key custodian for CMKs when we choose BYOK (customer-managed key) — specifically: do you require any escrow or hold a copy?
- Operator access model: what exact actions can Redwood engineers perform on a private (on-prem/VPC) deployment and under what auth model?
- Subprocessor disclosure (we need a CSV of subprocessors and whether they may access logs)

Can you send an annotated DPA and network/ops diagram that shows the data flow and the points where Redwood has any visibility? Also need timeline for SOC/audit artifacts the procurement team may request.

-Sam
Sam Patel
Sr. IT Security Manager
Veridian Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on DPA boundaries & BYOK for private deployment
Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf (application/pdf), subprocessor_list_2026.csv (text/csv)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current DPA draft (v3) and the up-to-date subprocessor CSV. High-level answers below; Irene and Ben are looped in for operational/legal detail.

1) Territory / transfers
- For private deployments we support region pinning. Data stored in your VPC (or on-prem) remains in your environment; Redwood does not move customer data outside the configured region except for explicitly agreed backups or disaster recovery where you opt in.
- Cross-border backups are considered an export and would be reflected in the DPA: we propose an Annex that requires written customer authorization for cross-border replication.

2) BYOK / CMK responsibilities
- Customer owns the key material. We do not retain plaintext keys. For most private deployments the recommended pattern is: customer provision CMK in their KMS, Redwood is granted a binding service account with Encrypt/Decrypt limited to the deployed runtime.
- We can offer an optional key-escrow workflow for customers that require escrow; this is an addendum and will include strict access controls and notarized custody steps. Default stance: no escrow unless explicitly signed.

3) Operator access model
- Redwood engineers do not have interactive shell access to customer compute in private VPCs. Support actions are performed via an RBAC service account created in your environment; operations are auditable and require approval.
- We offer a documented break-glass procedure for emergency key recovery; this is logged and requires two-person authorization.

4) Subprocessors
- See attached CSV for current subprocessors and roles. None of the listed subprocessors have access to customer plaintext data for private deployments by default; access would be scoped and logged per the DPA.

Next steps: please confirm (a) whether Veridian wants cross-border replication blocked by default, and (b) whether you require escrow or prefer pure customer-held keys. If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min call with Ben (ops) and Irene (legal) to walk the team through the annex language.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@veridianhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on DPA boundaries & BYOK for private deployment

Sam — quick ops note to supplement Evelyn's email:

- The RBAC service account pattern we propose maps to a managed IAM role in your cloud account (we provide a CloudFormation/Terraform template). The service account only has the APIs needed to call the inference runtime and to update model bundles — no access to underlying customer buckets unless you explicitly grant.
- Audit logs (API call traces + model inference traces metadata) are forwarded to your logging sink; Redwood retains a minimal operational copy for 30 days for troubleshooting (can be configured shorter).
- For SOC evidence: we can provide redacted runbooks, proof of encryption at rest, and a recent SOC2 Type II report for hosted control plane only. For private/on-prem we can deliver an evidence package tailored to the deployed topology; lead time ~7 business days.

If Veridian requires an explicit prohibition on any outbound replication, we can set the default policy to deny replication unless a signed annex is provided.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@veridianhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on DPA boundaries & BYOK for private deployment

Sam,

Adding legal context here (Irene Choi, Privacy & Compliance). A few clarifications I recommend for the DPA annex language so procurement can sign quickly:

- Explicit Data Location Clause: "Customer Data processed in Customer-controlled infrastructure will not be transferred to any location outside the specified region without Customer's prior written consent."
- Key Custody Clause: "Customer retains sole custody of key material; Redwood will not require, hold, or escrow customer encryption keys except where an Escrow Addendum is executed outlining custody and access procedures."
- Subprocessor Access Controls: include a table listing subprocessors, purpose, and whether they may access logs. For private deployments, mark all as "no access to plaintext unless emergency break-glass invoked and pre-authorized".
- Audit & Evidence: define the artifacts Redwood will provide (redacted logs, runbook, template SOC evidence) and the SLA for delivery (7 business days after request).

I will prepare suggested DPA redlines and a short Annex template that implements the above. Evelyn — can you confirm whether Veridian wants replication blocked by default? If yes we'll draft a single-line clause for the Annex.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam@veridianhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jill Thompson <jill@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on DPA boundaries & BYOK for private deployment
Attachments: network_diagram_v2.png (image/png)

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers from our side:

- Replication: block by default. We will not permit cross-border replication without a signed Annex.
- Keys: we prefer pure customer-held keys with no escrow. We may revisit escrow for legal continuity, but only under a separate negotiated addendum.
- Operator access: break-glass allowed but must be time-limited, justification logged, and require two Redwood approvers plus Veridian notification.

Two follow-ups: 1) can you add a short clause that states backups taken for DR are encrypted with the customer's CMK and held in the same region unless explicitly authorized? 2) for the subprocessor CSV — can you verify that any telemetry pipeline that touches logs is included and whether any third parties (e.g., managed monitoring vendors) receive those logs? I've attached an internal network diagram for reference.

If you can send the redlines and the Annex template by Monday, procurement will take it to Legal. Appreciated.

-Sam
Sr. IT Security Manager
Veridian Health
